title: The Last Call
premise: Two friends share a final phone call the night before one of them leaves the city for good. What was left unsaid finally surfaces.

rights.basis: Work made for the platform; no third-party film audio or script.

situation_before: Maya and Jordan have been best friends since school. Jordan is moving overseas tomorrow. They have avoided a real goodbye.

characters.name: Maya
characters.description: Warm, guarded, stays in the city. Wants honesty before Jordan leaves.
characters.objective: Get Jordan to admit this friendship still matters before the call ends.
characters.obstacles: Fear of seeming needy; Jordan deflects with humour.

characters.name: Jordan
characters.description: Leaving at dawn. Uses lightness to avoid grief.
characters.objective: Keep the goodbye light so neither of them falls apart.
characters.obstacles: Maya will not accept a shallow farewell.

relationship: Lifelong friends; romantic tension never named.
director_note: Keep it intimate and conversational. Silence is part of the scene. Do not rush the final beat.

dialogue.text: Hey. I wasn't sure you'd pick up this late.
Of course I picked up. You leave in six hours.
Don't make it sound like a funeral. It's just a job.
It's not just a job, Jordan. It's the end of us living on the same street.
We'll call. Video. Time zones are just maths.
Maths doesn't replace the way you knock on my door when the power goes out.
Then say it. Say you'll miss this. Not the city. This.
I'll miss you, Maya. More than I planned to.
Good. Now go pack. And text me from the airport — not a joke. A real text.
